the-name.body:
The ​name is ‌attested in ‌Greek ​as **Φάνης**. ​Etymologically ​it means ​"Bringer of ​light"[^1].

‌The ASCII ​form *phanes* ​survives ‌only because ​the ‌early domain-name ​system could ‌not ​carry diacritics; ​it is ​a ​technological compromise, ​not ‌an ancient ​spelling. The ‌Unicode ​restoration **Phánēs** ‌recovers both ​the ‌stress accent ​and ‌the vowel ​length of ​the ‌original directly ‌in the ‌address ​bar. The ​original ‌carries both ​stress and ​vowel ‌length, and ​exactly one ​historically ‌valid Unicode ​restoration ‌exists, which ​places the ​name ​in Tier ​1.

The ‌letter-by-letter ‌transformation runs:

​- ‌**p** → ​**P** — ​P ‌uppercase
- ‌**h** → ‌**h** ‌— h ​same
‌- **a** ​→ **á** ​— ​Acute on ‌a
- ​**n** ​→ **n** ​— ‌n same
​- **e** ​→ ​**ē** — ‌Macron: long ​vowel
‌- **s** ​→ ‌**s** — ​s same

‌The ‌project holds ​the domain ​**phánēs.com** ​(xn--phns-6na51a.com) as ​the ‌canonical home ‌of this ​name[^2].

sources.citation: Orphic Hymns.
Derveni Papyrus.

overview.body:
**Phánēs** ​(*phanes*) — ‌The ‌First Shining ​One ​— belongs ​to ​the Greek ​tradition, ‌where it ​is ​catalogued under ‌the ​domain "Procreation, ‌Light". ​The name ‌means ​"Bringer of ​light"[^1].

​Phánēs is ​the ​hidden first ‌god of ​the ‌Orphic theogonies: ​hatched ‌from the ​silver ‌egg of ​Time, ‌winged and ​shining, ​the first ‌form ‌in which ‌the ​universe could ​see ‌itself. Zeús ​himself ​will swallow ‌him ​— and ​in ‌swallowing, become ​everything.[^2]

‌PuniCodex restores ​the ​name as ​**Phánēs** ​and serves ‌its ‌temple at ​[phánēs.com](https://xn--phns-6na51a.com). ‌The original ​carries ​both stress ‌and ‌vowel length, ‌and ‌exactly one ​historically ‌valid Unicode ​restoration ​exists, which ​places ‌the name ​in Tier ​1. ​The plain ‌ASCII ​form *phanes* ​survives ​as a ‌modern ​convenience imposed ‌by ​the early ‌domain-name ​system; the ‌restoration, ‌not the ​fallback, ​is the ​form ​the project ‌defends ‌as philologically ​complete[^3].

domains.body:
Phánēs ​is ‌the hidden ‌first ​god ​of the ​Orphic ​theogonies: ​hatched ‌from the ​silver ​egg ‌of Time, ​winged ‌and ​shining, ‌the first ​form ​in ​which the ​universe ​could ‌see ​itself. Zeús ‌himself ​will ‌swallow him ​— ‌and ​in ‌swallowing, become ​everything.[^1]

​### ‌The Silver ‌Egg

‌Formed ​by ​Chronos in ‌the ​aithēr; ​from it ‌the ​shining ​one ‌hatches with ​golden ‌wings.

​### ​Protogonos

"First-born" ​— ​his ‌other name; ‌also ​Erikepaios, ‌Mētis, ​and bright-winged ​Erōs.

‌### ‌The Swallowing

‌Zeús ‌devours ​Phánēs ‌and with ​him ​all ​that is: ‌sky, ​earth, ​sea, ​and the ‌blessed ​gods.

​### The ​Key ‌of ​Mind

‌Orphic verse ​calls ‌him ​"the key ‌of ‌the ​mind" ​— the ​first ​intelligence ‌to shine ‌in ​darkness.

epithets.body:
The ​Orphic ‌tradition ‌gives him ​more ​names ​than ​any ​other ‌god ​— the ​theology ‌of ​the ‌many-named ​first ‌principle.

​- **Πρωτόγονος ​(Prōtógonos)** ​— ​'First-born'; ​his ‌formal ​title ‌in the ​Derveni ‌papyrus ​and ‌the ​Rhapsodies.
‌- **Ἠρικεπαῖος ​(Ērikepaîos)** ​— ‌the ‌untranslatable ‌ritual ​name, ​possibly 'life-giver'; ‌his ​mystery ​invocation.
‌- ​**Φαέθων ​(Phaéthōn)** ‌— 'the ​Shining'; ‌the ​name ​his ​own ​name ‌glosses.
- ‌**Μῆτις ​(Mêtis)** ‌— ​'Counsel'; ​the ‌Orphic ‌equation of ‌first ‌light ​with ‌first ​wisdom.
​- **Ἔρως ​(Érōs)** ‌— ​Hesiod's ​oldest ​power, ‌absorbed ​into the ​Orphic ​first ‌god.
​- ‌**Διόνυσος ​(Diónysos)** ‌— in ​the ‌Orphic ‌succession, ​Phánēs ​is ​Dionysos ​in his ‌first, ‌pre-Zagreus ​form.

sources.citation: Orphic Fragments (Kern) 60–167; Derveni Papyrus col. XIII–XXVI.

mythology.body:
Phánēs belongs to ​the other Greece — ‌the Orphic theogonies sung ‌by initiates, where the ​cosmos begins not with ​Chaos' yawn but with ​an egg, and the ​first god is light ​itself given a name.[^1]

‌### Born of the ​Egg (The Hatching)

In ​the Orphic Rhapsodies, Chronos ‌— Time unaging — ​fashions a silver egg ‌in the divine aithēr. ​The egg splits, and Phánēs ‌emerges: double-sexed, four-eyed, golden-winged, ​a bull-roarer here, a ​serpent there, "the first-born, ​the revealer," who brings ​light to the blessed ​gods and gives birth ‌to the race of ​immortals.[^2]

### Fourth King ‌of the Gods (The ​Sovereignty)

The Orphic succession ‌differs from Hesiod's: after ​Ouranós and Kronos, Phánēs ‌holds the sceptre — ​fourth king, before Zeús. He ‌creates the sun and ​moon, founds the first ​Olympus, and rules a ‌cosmos that is still, ‌as the hymns say, ‌"all in one."

### ​Zeús Becomes All (The ​Swallowing)

The supreme Orphic ‌mystery: Zeús swallows Phánēs ​whole, and with him ​the entire first creation. ‌The preserved fragment marvels ​— "thus all things ​were made anew within ‌Zeús: sky, earth, sea, the ​stars, and the blessed ‌gods" — and the ​cosmos is born a ​second time from the ​king's body. Creation is ​not once but twice: ‌first revealed, then reabsorbed ‌and reborn.

### The ​Derveni Commentary (The Papyrus)

‌The Derveni papyrus — ​Europe's oldest surviving book, ​carbonized in a Macedonian ‌funeral pyre around 340 ‌BCE — quotes the ‌Orphic poem about Protogonos and ‌glosses him as "Mind": ​the first thing to ‌leap forth. It proves ​the Phánēs theology was ​already old, already allegorized, ​before Plato wrote a ‌word.

### Instructions for ​the Dead (The Tablets)

​The Orphic gold tablets, ​buried with initiates from ‌Thessaly to South Italy, ​coach the soul for ​the underworld: avoid the ​spring of forgetfulness, drink from ‌the lake of memory, ​and say to the ‌guardians, "I am a ​child of Earth and ‌starry Heaven; but my ​race is of Heaven ‌alone." The tablets never ‌name Phánēs — but ​their cosmology is his: ​the initiate's soul, like ​the first-shining one, claims ​descent from light, and ‌the journey of the ‌dead replays the hatching ​of the world.

meditation.body:
Phánēs ​is the ‌god of ‌first ​versions — ​the ​shining draft ​that must ​be ‌swallowed and ​rewritten ​before the ‌world can ​be ‌published. Every ​creator knows ‌him: ​the first ​form ​of anything ​true is ​radiant, ‌total, and ​unusable, ‌and only ​its sacrifice ‌makes ​the durable ‌cosmos. ​He asks ‌a hard ​question: ​what are ‌you willing ‌to ‌swallow of ​your ​first light ‌so that ​something ​greater can ‌be ​born?

The ​Orphic initiates ‌buried ​with their ‌gold tablets ​understood ​him as ​instruction, ​not cosmology: ‌remember that ‌you ​are hatched ‌from ​light, and ​the dark ‌of ‌the grave ‌is only ‌the ​egg's second ‌shell. ​That is ​why his ​cult ‌left no ​temples ​and his ​myth left ‌no ​images — ​the ​first-shining one ‌is not ​worshipped ‌but recognized, ​in every ‌first ​draft, every ‌first ‌light, every ​beginning that ​must ​be swallowed ​before ‌the real ‌world can ​begin.[^1]

pronunciation.body:
The ​reconstructed ‌pronunciation of ‌the ​name ​is **/pʰá.nɛːs/** ​— ​Attic ​Greek.[^1]

For ‌the ​modern ​speaker, ‌the closest ​approximation ‌is: ​FAH-nace, stress ‌on ​the ​first ​syllable with ​a ​long ‌ē.

Kindred ​and ‌historical ​forms of ‌the ​name:

‌- ​**Greek** — ‌Φάνης
​- ​**Orphic title** ‌— ‌Πρωτόγονος
‌- ​**Owned form** ​— ‌Phánēs

​Phánēs takes ​his ‌name ​from the ​verb ‌φαίνω, ​"to ‌bring to ​light, ​to ​reveal" — ​the ‌same ‌root as ​"phenomenon" ‌and ​"epiphany." ​The accent ‌is ‌recessive ‌on the ‌first ​syllable; ‌the ​long ē ​of ​the ‌second syllable ​is ​what ​the macron ‌preserves ​in ​the ​restoration. The ‌Orphic ​hymns ‌scan the ​name ‌as ​two ‌syllables, stress ‌on ​the ​first; the ​Latin ​poets ‌wrote it ‌Phanes ​unchanged.
